The Opportunity:
Maitland City Council's Pathways program is a fantastic way to kick-start your career and gain professional experience in local government!
Commencing in January 2027, for a period of two years, we have two exciting opportunities for Graduate Civil Engineers to join our organisation.
In this role, you will undertake a graduate program developed specifically for you, giving you exposure to a range of civil engineering functions for the investigation and delivery of civil and recreation infrastructure projects undertaken by Council. These duties are going to help you develop a solid foundation to your civil engineering career.
About you:
To be successful in this role you will possess:
- Degree level qualifications in Civil engineering in the previous two years or completion of degree by January 2027
- Contemporary industry knowledge of civil engineering areas
- Experience and understanding in project support and the research, analysis and presentation of information
- Current Class C driver's licence
Benefits:
This Graduate position is temporary full time (two-year contract) with a commencing salary of $1,414.58 weekly, plus 12% superannuation. Graduates will also have access to Council's great staff benefits including:
- Flexible work arrangements
- One extra week of "My Leave" a year (to use how you like!)
- Ongoing training and development
- Fitness Passport
- Healthy Employee Program
To apply:
To apply for this opportunity, please click 'Apply Now' and submit your resume and cover letter.
Questions:
To viw the role charter click 'Apply Now'. If after reading the role charter you have any questions, please contact the recruitment team at Recruitment@maitland.nsw.gov.au
More information regarding Council's Pathways Program can be viewed via https://www.maitland.nsw.gov.au/pathways-program.
Applications close: Sunday 25th October 2027
Only candidates with current Australian work rights (Australian citizens, permanent residents, NZ citizens with a current passport, valid work visa) will be considered.

Once applications close, we will review all candidates' details against the role requirements and will be back in touch with you to advise the status of your application.

For more information about the recruitment process, visit the "Jobs at Council" page on our website.

candidates.content_text:
Build your career with an organisation that is invested in your success. 
Maker Consulting Services is looking for a motivated Civil Engineering Undergraduate or Graduate to join our growing Newcastle team. Whether you're currently studying and looking to gain meaningful industry experience alongside university; or completing your degree and ready to begin your graduate career, this role offers the opportunity to develop your technical skills while contributing to real projects from day one. 
You'll work alongside experienced engineers on land development, infrastructure, roads and stormwater projects across Newcastle, the Hunter and broader NSW, gaining practical experience that complements your university studies and builds the foundation for your professional career. 
At Maker, we believe in providing a flexible work lifestyle. This has inspired us to change the way we work, leaving behind the traditional 5-day work week. Instead, Maker has adopted a 4-day work week, providing you with a day off during the week and giving you the time to catch up on life and do more of what you love!  
For undergraduate candidates, we offer flexibility around university timetables and exam periods, allowing you to gain consistent industry experience while completing your degree. 
Why join Maker 
Maker is a fast-growing, multi-disciplinary consultancy with more than 65 employees across 4 offices in NSW and Victoria. In addition to Civil Engineering, we specialise in Town Planning, Surveying, and Project Management which provides you with the opportunity to collaborate across a wide range of exciting projects. 
You’ll enjoy:
- Hands-on mentoring from experienced civil engineers, including direct exposure to senior members of our Newcastle team.  
- Real project involvement from the outset - not just observation or administrative tasks.  
- Experience across land development, roads, stormwater, infrastructure and multidisciplinary projects.  
- Opportunities to develop your skills in industry-standard civil design and modelling software.  
- A supportive culture where questions are encouraged and knowledge is shared. 
- The opportunity to grow from undergraduate engineer through to graduate and increasingly independent project responsibilities.  
- A 4-day working week, giving you more time to enjoy life outside work 
- Modern offices and regular team social events 
About the Role 
Located in our Newcastle office and working closely with our Newcastle Principal Civil Engineer, you will be exposed to a variety of projects that will introduce you to a broad range of civil engineering disciplines and progressively build your technical and professional capability. 
Your responsibilities will include: 
- Assisting with the design and documentation of civil infrastructure and land development projects, including roads, earthworks, stormwater drainage and utility infrastructure. 
- Developing practical experience using industry-standard civil design and modelling software. 
- Assisting with engineering calculations, technical assessments and preparation of reports. 
- Working with engineers, surveyors, planners and project managers to understand how projects progress from concept through to construction. 
- Participating in site inspections, project meetings and coordination activities where appropriate. 
You'll be encouraged to ask questions, learn from experienced professionals and progressively take on greater responsibility as your confidence grows. 
For undergraduate candidates, our aim is to provide meaningful, ongoing employment throughout your studies, with flexible part-time arrangements to suit university commitments and the opportunity to transition into a graduate position as you complete your degree. 
About You 
We're looking for someone curious, motivated and excited to build a career in Civil Engineering. 
We're looking for:
- Someone currently studying a Bachelor's degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering, or who has recently graduated from a relevant engineering degree. 
- A genuine interest in civil engineering and a willingness to learn. 
- An interest in design, problem-solving and seeing projects progress from concept through to construction. 
- Good written and verbal communication skills, with an interest in developing your technical writing capability. 
- Good time management, organisation and prioritisation skills. 
- The ability to work both independently and as part of a collaborative team. 
Whether you're part-way through your degree and looking to build industry experience alongside your studies, or approaching graduation and ready to begin your professional career, we'd like to hear from you. 
Ready to Build Your Career? 
If you're looking to gain meaningful civil engineering experience while completing your degree, or you're ready to take the first step in your graduate career, we'd love to hear from you. 
Please submit your resume and a short cover letter telling us a little about yourself, your studies and why you're interested in joining Maker by clicking the APPLY button.

- Exposure to roads, drainage, stormwater, water, subdivisions or similar projects
- Strong technical and problem-solving skills
- Good attention to detail and an ability to manage competing priorities
- Clear written and verbal communication skills
- A practical approach to engineering and project delivery
- Current driver's licence and willingness to attend project sites

They offer the opportunity to work alongside experienced Civil Engineers and project professionals on projects across both metropolitan and regional environments. The business places a strong emphasis on professional development, practical experience, integrity and delivering quality outcomes for its clients.

- $75,000 - $85,000 + super, negotiable based on experience
- Relocation assistance available
- Diverse civil projects from concept and design through to construction
- Exposure to roads, drainage, water, infrastructure and land development
- Hands-on project and site experience
- Mentoring from experienced senior engineers
- Ongoing training and professional development
- Opportunity to contribute ideas and influence project outcomes
- Supportive and collaborative team environment
- Long-term career stability and genuine project variety
How To Apply
To build your career with a company that values quality engineering, practical solutions and the work you deliver, please click Apply and please include any civil design experience you have undertaken in your application.
About Us
With Head Office in Cairns and offices in Townsville and Brisbane. We specialise in professional, administration, engineering and industrial recruitment, permanent and temporary placements for both commercial and government enterprise. We are proud to connect great people with meaningful careers.

- Work on a landmark civil infrastructure project from day one
- Gain exposure to multiple disciplines across project delivery
- Receive structured mentoring, coaching and development support
- Learn from experienced industry leaders and subject matter experts
- Build a strong professional network across projects and regions
- Be part of a collaborative, supportive and high-performing team culture
- Access career opportunities within the VINCI Group, a global leader in construction, infrastructure and concessions

- Practical experience through internships, vacation programs, placements or other employment

- A positive attitude and willingness to learn from experienced industry professionals
- Strong communication and teamwork skills
- A commitment to safety, collaboration and creating a positive team culture
- Flexibility to travel or relocate as opportunities arise throughout your career

If you're ready to learn, grow and help shape the future, we'd love to hear from you.

We have an exciting opportunity for a Graduate Civil Engineer to join our Cressbrook Dam Safety Improvement Project, a major infrastructure upgrade that will strengthen the dam's flood capacity, improve resilience to extreme weather events and enhance long-term community safety.
This is a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience on a complex and high-profile project while working alongside experienced industry professionals. You'll be exposed to a broad range of civil engineering disciplines and play a meaningful role in delivering infrastructure that will benefit local communities for generations to come.
Located in the picturesque Toowoomba region, this role offers the chance to build your career in a supportive project environment while enjoying the benefits of regional living.
The successful candidate will be required to work away from home, with attractive living away from home (LAFHA) and project allowances provided.
Why Join Seymour Whyte?
At Seymour Whyte, we believe the best way to learn is by doing. Our structured Graduate Development Program is designed to fast-track your career through hands-on project experience, mentoring from industry leaders and tailored professional development opportunities.
From day one, you'll be embedded in a live project team, contributing to the delivery of major infrastructure projects that shape communities across Australia. You'll gain exposure to a range of disciplines, build your technical and commercial acumen and develop the confidence to take ownership of meaningful work early in your career.
Throughout the program, you'll be supported by experienced mentors, participate in structured development workshops, and connect with a national network of graduates and professionals who are invested in your success.
What's in it for you?
- Work on a landmark civil infrastructure project from day one
- Gain exposure to multiple disciplines across project delivery
- Receive structured mentoring, coaching and development support
- Learn from experienced industry leaders and subject matter experts
- Build a strong professional network across projects and regions
- Be part of a collaborative, supportive and high-performing team culture
- Access career opportunities within the VINCI Group, a global leader in construction, infrastructure and concessions
Whether your passion lies in construction delivery, engineering, project management or leadership, our Graduate Development Program will provide the foundation, support and opportunities to help you build a rewarding and long-term career with Seymour Whyte.
To learn more about our Graduate Program, click here.

You're in your final year of a Bachelor of Civil Engineering and ready to turn everything you've learned into real-world experience on major infrastructure projects.
Whether you've gained experience through an internship, vacation work, industry placement or part-time employment, you're eager to learn, build your skills and make a meaningful contribution from day one.
We're looking for graduates who are curious, motivated and excited about a career in civil construction.

- Final-year studies in a Bachelor of Civil Engineering
- Practical experience through internships, vacation programs, placements or other employment
- A genuine passion for civil construction and infrastructure projects
- A positive attitude and willingness to learn from experienced industry professionals
- Strong communication and teamwork skills
- A commitment to safety, collaboration and creating a positive team culture

Most importantly, you're ready to take the next step, embrace new challenges and build a rewarding career delivering projects that make a lasting impact on communities across Australia.

Our commitment to an equitable construction industry extends to an inclusive culture that embraces our differences and gives everyone the opportunity to grow and be equally valued. We're unified in our direction toward having a workplace that is balanced and fair for all.

About Us
For over 35 years, GPA Engineering has been a trusted, Australian-owned consultancy delivering engineering, procurement and construction management services across water, energy, renewables, defence, mining, and hydrogen. We develop and implement projects that drive critical infrastructure and support industries across Australia.
With offices nationwide (Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Sydney, Darwin, Perth) and a reputation for technical excellence, our strength lies in our people. We bring together diverse, motivated professionals who value teamwork, integrity, safety, and sustainability. At GPA, you’ll find the scale and expertise of a leading consultancy, combined with the supportive culture of a close-knit team.
About the Role
With a strong pipeline of projects across the energy, resources and industrial sectors, GPA Engineering is seeking an experienced Civil/Structural Drafter to join our Adelaide team.
Based in our Adelaide Head Office, you will work as part of a multidisciplinary team delivering projects across oil & gas, mining, materials handling, water and power. This role is suited to someone with 3-10 years' experience who enjoys variety, technical challenges and developing high-quality 2D drawings and 3D models.
Working closely with engineers and designers, you'll contribute to projects from concept through to detailed design, gaining exposure to a broad range of clients and industries. You'll have the opportunity to further develop your drafting and modelling skills while taking increasing ownership of design documentation and model coordination.
Key Duties:
 - Prepare, revise and maintain civil and structural engineering drawings and 3D models across a range of projects.
 - Produce high-quality 2D deliverables including general arrangements, plans, elevations, sections and construction details.
 - Develop and maintain 3D models to support coordinated multidisciplinary project delivery.
 - Work closely with engineers and designers to translate engineering concepts and calculations into clear and practical design documentation.
 - Apply relevant Australian Standards, client specifications, project requirements and GPA drafting standards.
 - Participate in drawing and model reviews and incorporate design changes and review comments.
 - Coordinate with other engineering disciplines to identify and resolve design interfaces and clashes.
 - Manage assigned drafting activities to meet project schedules and agreed deliverables.
 - Ensure drawings, models and associated documentation comply with GPA quality assurance requirements
We are looking for a collaborative and technically capable Civil/Structural Drafter with strong attention to detail and a practical approach to engineering documentation.
The successful candidate will ideally have:
 - Qualifications: An Associate Degree in Civil and Structural Engineering (Design Drafting), Advanced Diploma or equivalent recognised drafting/design qualification, either completed or currently being undertaken.
 - Experience: Approximately 3–10 years of relevant civil and/or structural drafting and design experience earthworks.
 - Industry Experience: Experience in heavy industry sectors such as oil & gas, mining, materials handling, water or power will be highly regarded.
 - 2D Drafting: Strong capability in producing engineering drawings including general arrangements, plans, elevations, sections and construction details.
 - 3D Modelling: Experience developing and working with 3D models as part of coordinated engineering project delivery.
 - Software: Proficiency in AutoCAD and/or MicroStation. Experience with Civil 3D, Advance Steel, Revit or other relevant design and modelling software would be advantageous.
 - Technical Understanding: Ability to interpret engineering mark-ups, design information, relevant Australian Standards and client specifications.
 - Quality: Strong attention to detail and an understanding of engineering drawing standards, document control and QA processes.
 - Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively both independently and within multidisciplinary project teams.
A requirement for this role is to complete a satisfactory pre-employment medical check and Australian police clearance. 
At GPA, we want our people to thrive both professionally and personally. We’re big enough to deliver complex, high-profile projects, yet small enough that you’ll be known, valued and supported.
 - Competitive Salary & Rewards – an attractive remuneration package, including paid overtime, recognising the value of the work you put in.
 - Career Growth & Development – structured career progression, company-sponsored training, mentoring and support towards professional membership and Chartership.
 - Diverse Project Exposure – opportunities to work across different industries, clients and project types, building broad technical and practical experience.
 - Flexibility – hybrid working options and cultural leave swap days, supporting a healthy balance between work and life.
 - Health & Wellbeing – wellbeing programs, confidential EAP support and a workplace culture that looks out for its people.
 - Family-Friendly Benefits – paid parental leave for primary and secondary carers, together with policies designed to support different stages of life.
 - Community & Culture – opportunities to connect beyond project work through sporting and fitness groups, social events, family BBQs, quiz nights and celebrations of diverse cultural traditions.
 - Giving Back – a strong commitment to the community, with GPA having donated more than $3 million directly to charitable organisations.
 - Diversity & Inclusion – a workplace where different perspectives are respected and collaboration is encouraged.
At GPA, we offer a supportive working environment where people can build long-term careers. More than 80 of our team members have been with GPA for over 10 years, reflecting the opportunities, culture and stability we aim to provide.
Hear from our people and learn more about working at GPA through our Careers page (https://www.gpaeng.com.au/careers/).
GPA is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences.

Submit your applications through our online recruitment system before EOD 30th October 2026.

City of Armadale
Armadale, Perth WA
Engineering – Civil/Structural Engineering 
$102,000–$117,000 per annum plus superannuation
Shape a growing City’s infrastructure. Plan capital projects through design, costing and approvals, with WFH and flexi-time for a 9-day fortnight.
 -  Shape infrastructure projects across asset renewal, upgrades and growth.
 -  Flexible working with WFH and accrued flexi-time towards a 9-day fortnight.
 -  Superannuation up to 15%, subject to conditions, plus free gym membership.
 Help shape the projects that shape our City
Good infrastructure starts with good decisions. Understanding what is needed, testing the options and resolving the detail before construction begins.
At the City of Armadale, you’ll help make those decisions. As one of Western Australia’s fastest-growing local governments, we’re planning new infrastructure while improving and renewing the assets our community already relies on.
We’re looking for a Project Planning Engineer who brings practical judgement, asks good questions and takes pride in preparing projects properly.
If you’re enjoying your current role but would welcome the opportunity to influence a growing City’s infrastructure, this could be your next move.
Why Armadale?
Our Strategic Community Plan sets a clear direction: facilities that meet community needs, better public places, and infrastructure that is functional, inclusive and sustainable.
You’ll help turn those priorities into practical projects, balancing technical requirements, cost, risk and long-term asset performance. Across renewal, upgrade and growth projects, you’ll tackle varied challenges and see how your work contributes to the community.
You’ll also have flexibility in how you work, including working from home and the ability to accrue flexi-time to work a nine-day fortnight, with arrangements agreed around role and team requirements.
Your role
Working in our Asset Planning team, reporting to the Project Planning Lead, you’ll progress identified infrastructure priorities into well-defined, costed and approved capital projects ready for delivery.
Starting with Project Initiation Documents developed by Strategic Asset Management, you’ll coordinate investigations and detailed designs, refine cost estimates and progress the approvals needed for capital works program entry.
You’ll work with engineering and landscape design specialists, consultants, asset operators and delivery teams to:
 - Develop clear project scopes, specifications and budget requirements.
 - Coordinate investigations, technical advice and detailed design activities.
 - Prepare and refine cost estimates, checking assumptions, contingencies and constructability.
 - Progress approvals, utility clearances, statutory consents and other project requirements.
 - Prepare complete project packages for review under the City’s Project Management Framework.
 - Resolve risks and gaps early, considering procurement, construction sequencing and handover requirements.
Your work will help the City make informed investment decisions and give delivery teams confidence in each project’s scope, cost and readiness.
What you’ll bring
You know what it takes to prepare an infrastructure project for delivery. You can work through technical detail, challenge assumptions constructively and bring the right people together to resolve issues.
We’re looking for:
 - Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering, Project Management, Construction Management or a closely related discipline**, or equivalent demonstrated experience in project planning and infrastructure development.
 - Experience planning civil infrastructure or construction projects.
 - Sound knowledge of cost estimation, contingency allowances and key cost drivers.
 - The ability to coordinate technical input across disciplines and progress third-party approvals.
 - Familiarity with project management frameworks and project approval requirements.
Flexibility and benefits
 - Working-from-home arrangements and flexi-time, including the ability to accrue time towards a nine-day fortnight.
 - Superannuation contributions of up to 15%, subject to employee contributions and applicable conditions.
 - Free Armadale Fitness and Aquatic Centre membership**, including the gym, pools, sauna and group fitness classes.
 - Wellbeing activities throughout the year.
 - Novated leasing opportunities.
Our values—Care; Are Better, Together; Learn & Grow; and Seize Today, Shape Tomorrow—guide how we work. We listen, share knowledge and welcome people who bring ideas and take responsibility for their work.
Interested? Let’s talk
You don’t need to be actively looking for a new job to explore this opportunity.
For an initial confidential conversation, contact People Services on 9394 5189 or hr@armadale.wa.gov.au. 
Ready to apply? Submit your CV and a brief cover letter through the application link, outlining your relevant experience and interest in the role.
We review applications as they are received and may close the advertisement early.
*The City of Armadale welcomes applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, people from culturally diverse backgrounds and people of all genders and identities.*
*We are committed to child safety and recruitment practices that support a safe and inclusive community.*

- Someone who enjoys working with others and being part of a team.

Help shape stormwater’s next chapter.

Our purpose
At Rain, we exist to support, challenge and lift ourselves, each other and the people we work with.
That means helping clients understand their options and giving them the clarity and confidence to act. It also means backing our own people to develop their judgement, take ownership and contribute to how the industry works.
We value creative thinking, especially when it leads to a sound, practical solution.
How we work
Our values guide our decisions and the standards we hold ourselves to:
- Quality: We check assumptions, review our work and explain the findings clearly.
- Integrity: We give honest advice, including when a client needs to hear something difficult.
- Stewardship: We consider what our decisions mean for communities and the environment over the long term.
You’ll work with major clients, including City of Melbourne and Melbourne Water, as part of a small team where your contribution is visible.
You’ll have direct support from Luke and Rianda, Rain’s Directors, and colleagues who want to see you develop. As your capability grows, there’s room to take on greater responsibility and build your own voice in the industry.
We welcome questions, thoughtful challenges and ideas for doing things better. You’ll be trusted to contribute, with technical review and support around you.
The role is Melbourne-based with hybrid working and flexibility, within a team that looks out for each other.
The problems you’ll help solve
A council is rethinking how it manages water across its community. A wetland or waterway needs a design that supports both people and the environment. A project needs a water balance to understand where water comes from, where it goes and how it could be used.
And behind each challenge, there are people who need help turning complex information into a clear way forward.
These are the kinds of questions you’ll work through at Rain.
You’ll use TUFLOW and RORB to investigate how water behaves, test options and understand their consequences. Your projects may also involve wetland and waterway design, water balances and integrated water management. You’ll turn that work into clear maps, reports and conversations that help people make sound decisions.
You’ll also get involved beyond the technical analysis. From shaping the brief to discussing the findings with the client, you’ll develop an understanding of what makes a project useful, achievable and worth doing. That includes managing scope, budgets and deadlines, with support from the team.
We want you to question assumptions and contribute ideas. If you see a better way to approach a problem, explain a result or manage water, there’s room to explore it with us.
As your confidence and capability grow, you’ll have opportunities to take greater ownership, guide others and contribute to our training or facilitation work.
The aim is for your contribution to keep helping people long after the report is delivered.
What you’ll bring
- An Engineering degree, including civil or environmental engineering, or an Environmental Science degree.
- 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience in flood, stormwater or water management.
- Solid practical TUFLOW and RORB skills.
- An understanding of hydrologic, hydraulic and stormwater processes.
- The ability to plan your work, take responsibility and ask for support when you need it.
- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical findings to different audiences.
- Curiosity about better ways of doing things and care for the quality and impact of your work.
Experience with MUSIC and QGIS is valuable. Training, facilitation or mentoring experience is a bonus.
Your next move
Send your CV and a short note about why you’d like to work at Rain to hiring@rainconsulting.com.au.
Tell us about the work you’ve done, the work you’d like to do next and what you’d bring to the team.
You’re also welcome to email us if you’d like to ask a question before applying.

 Working closely with the Construction Manager, Project Manager and site delivery teams, you will play a critical role in ensuring construction activities meet engineering specifications, Australian Standards, quality requirements and statutory obligations.
 We are particularly interested in engineers based in Mackay or Rockhampton who have extensive experience delivering major civil infrastructure projects and can regularly travel to Moranbah.
 Key Responsibilities - Provide RPEQ engineering oversight, technical verification and certification of civil construction works.

 - Verify compliance with approved drawings, engineering specifications, Australian Standards and project quality requirements.
 - Review Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), work packs, quality documentation and construction records.
 - Support inspections, hold points, engineering sign offs and construction verification.

 - Provide technical guidance to supervisors, engineers, contractors and project delivery teams.
 - Liaise with designers, construction management and project stakeholders to maintain engineering compliance and delivery standards.

 - Proven experience delivering major earthworks, rail formation, reinforced concrete bridges and culvert works.
 - Strong background in construction verification, technical oversight and engineering certification.
 - Sound understanding of Queensland engineering legislation, Australian Standards and construction compliance requirements.
 - Experience reviewing engineering drawings, methodologies, inspection records and quality documentation.
 - Strong technical leadership, problem solving and stakeholder management skills.
 - Construction White Card and current driver's licence.
 Highly Regarded

 - Previous involvement in major mining, transport or heavy civil infrastructure projects.
 - Experience working within operating rail environments.
 - Knowledge of earthworks testing, geotechnical requirements and formation construction.
 - Experience managing engineering compliance across multiple civil construction disciplines.

 We are working with a highly respected, Australian-owned engineering consultancy with an impressive global footprint and offices around the world. Their growing Sydney office is looking to welcome an experienced Structural Revit Drafter/BIM Technician to join the team.
 This is a fantastic opportunity to get involved in some seriously impressive projects! Think high-rise towers, iconic commercial developments, major mixed-use precincts and landmark buildings.
 The Sydney team is made up of some of the most talented structural engineers in the state, and with an incredibly strong pipeline of major projects already secured, you'll have the opportunity to get stuck into exciting work from day one.
 The Role
 You'll be joining a relatively small but growing structural drafting team in Sydney, which presents a brilliant opportunity for someone looking to make their mark and grow their career.
 You'll also be working with an awesome manager who is genuinely passionate about developing people. Someone who will mentor, guide, encourage and support you whenever needed, while giving you the autonomy and trust to do what you do best.
 As the Sydney office continues to grow, so will the opportunities for you to develop your skills, take on more responsibility and progress your career.
 Key Responsibilities
 - Develop and produce high-quality structural Revit models and detailed documentation for major building projects.
 - Work on large-scale developments including high-rise towers, commercial buildings and mixed-use precincts.
 - Collaborate closely with structural engineers, architects and other disciplines throughout the design and documentation process.
 - Produce detailed structural drawings covering reinforced concrete, structural steel and other building elements.
 - Coordinate BIM models and identify and resolve clashes and design coordination issues.
 - Contribute to the delivery of projects from concept design through to construction documentation.
 - Maintain high standards of modelling accuracy, quality and BIM compliance.
 - Work collaboratively with the wider engineering and drafting teams to deliver technically challenging projects.
 What We're Looking For
 - Experience as a Structural Revit Drafter, BIM Technician or Revit Modeller within a structural engineering consultancy.
 - Strong Revit modelling and structural documentation skills.
 - Experience working on building structures, ideally multi-storey, commercial or large-scale developments.
 - Good understanding of reinforced concrete and structural steel detailing.
 - Familiarity with BIM processes, coordination and model management.
 - Strong attention to detail and the ability to work collaboratively with engineers and other disciplines.
 - A positive attitude, willingness to learn and genuine enthusiasm for working on technically challenging projects.
 Experience working on large projects would be fantastic, but we're equally interested in speaking with talented structural drafters who are ready to take that next step and gain exposure to larger, more complex developments.
Why You'll Love This Opportunity
 - Large projects - Work on high-rise towers, landmark buildings and major developments.
 - Outstanding project pipeline - A strong pipeline of secured, large-scale projects ready for you to get involved in.
 - Work with the best - Collaborate with some of Sydney's most talented and experienced structural engineers.
 - Fantastic manager and mentor - Join a team led by someone who genuinely cares about your development, provides guidance and encourages you to succeed.
 - Small, growing drafting team - An exciting opportunity to make a real impact and grow alongside the Sydney business.
 - Genuine career progression - As the team expands, there will be opportunities to take on greater responsibility and develop your career.
 If you've been waiting for an opportunity to work on genuinely exciting projects, learn from some of the best engineers in the industry and be part of a growing team where your career can really take off, this could be exactly what you're looking for!
 Apply today or contact Natasha at Cookson & Roberts on 0410 777 473 for a confidential chat.
 All enquiries will be treated in the strictest confidence.
